newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end up on weather fears, spreading.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end up on weather fears, spreading.

text.p: Weather concerns added to bull spreading to keep CME live cattle futures strong at the close while feeder cattle ended up after an early technical rally in a short trading session, traders said.

Wintry weather is expected to move through the panhandle feedlot area of Texas by the weekend and this prompted nervous short covering support in live cattle futures. Bull spreading was also evident following firm live markets, they said.
Feedlots have kept marketings very current and fed cattle supplies will not be rising sufficently to press prices until next year, they added.
Refco bought December and February and sold April early. R.J. O'Brien was a net buyer while LIT division of First Options sold December early and E.D.&F. Man sold February, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, there was 3-way spreading in April, buying 64 puts and selling both 58 puts and 70 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder futures showed some profit taking resistance after running up early when carryover demand touched off buy stops. January hit stops when prices broke through the 40-day average at 65.600 cents, adding to the advance, traders said.
Corn futures trade influeced feeders at times. Higher corn prices early wighed on feeders but added to the advance later when they drifted lower, traders said.

The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.64 at $64.61 per cwt but appeared to have little influence on the market. Feeder prices will likely show overall strength in corn prices remain down and fed cattle prices hold firm, they added.
Live cattle finished 0.700 to 0.200 cent higher, with December up 0.700 at 66.800 cents a lb. Feeders finished 0.500 to 0.300 higher, with January up 0.475 at 65.675 cents.
Both contracts closed early at noon CST and will be closed Thursday in observance of U.S. Thanksgiving. The markets will also shut at noon CST Friday because of the holiday.
